creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`matches()` returns a bool and there is no capture or find-all API. Three structurally different workarounds arose independently across the corpus:

- Write to a temp file and shell out to `rg -oe`: `jmx:98-111`, roughly 14 lines plus a subprocess plus an `rg` dependency, in a script averaging 6.4 seconds.
- Guarded `replace()` abuse with `$1`: `jira-title-sync.rad:21-24`, `argus:232-233`, `dklogs:29`. Silently returns the input on no-match.
- Peel one match per loop iteration: `tag-macro.rad:23-30`.

Sketch from the reports: `match(s, pat) -> {match, groups}|null` and `find_all(s, pat, *, group=0)`.

Already tracked on the main board as "regex text match function", in `high`. Larger than the `escape_regex()` card in p0-tier1, which is why it sits here.

---

### Orientation

- New builtins are docs-first: the `## Signature` line in `docs/funcs/<name>.md` **is** the type-checker's signature. There is no parallel definition in Go. Read `docs/funcs/README.md` for the full file contract before writing anything.
- The regex engine is already Go's `regexp` (RE2). `core/func_matches.go` compiles the user pattern directly, and `core/func_replace.go` already exposes capture groups through `$1` substitution - so capture extraction is new surface, not new machinery.
- Runtime dispatch and arg binding live in `core/funcs.go`: a `FUNC_X` name const plus a `BuiltInFunc{Name, Execute}` entry in the registration slice.

### Watch out for

Go's RE2 has no backreferences or lookaround. Anyone reaching for capture extraction is likely coming from PCRE; the doc should say what is not supported rather than letting them discover it through a compile error.
title: Add regex capture extraction
